rappel_detail.notes: Below the rappel it is a scree and talus scramble worked rightward — clockwise around the peak, roughly south then west — back into the basin and the packs at the base of the west face. Terrain under the horn is low-angle enough that some parties downclimb it instead of rappelling.
rappel_detail.anchor: A natural horn wrapped in webbing / in-situ slings on the east side of the summit block. No bolts. It is re-slung periodically because it is the standard anchor for every CBR route that tops out here, so what you find will be a mix of ages.
hazards: The upper pitches and the ground around the summit block are loose and lichen-covered — the reason parties are advised to stay roped rather than solo across to the anchor
Single natural anchor on a high-traffic descent: inspect the webbing and add or replace your own before loading it
rappel_detail.station: From the top of the route, scramble across to the east side of the summit block; the slung horn is on that side and the rappel drops eastward. If you skip the balanced-rock boulder problem you can bypass the block entirely and never touch this anchor.

set.rappels: Over the top by the standard Colchuck Balanced Rock descent: one rappel of about 30 m east off a slung horn on the summit block (many parties downclimb it instead), then scree clockwise around the peak to the base.
set.descent_text: Parties who top out can use CBR's standard descent shared with the West Face: a single 30 m rappel east from a slung horn, then scree or snow clockwise around the peak to the base. The alternative, which avoids that loose ground, is to rappel the route itself: with two 60m ropes tied together, descend via a sequence of natural anchors — slung trees and horns down the crack systems below Launch Ledge — there are no bolts or fixed gear anywhere on the route, by design, so you are relying entirely on what you find or build (extra slings/cord are worth carrying). Watch for rope-snag risk in the corner systems on the crux Scoop pitch and loose rock low in the gully system if you bail before topping out. No count of rappels down the route itself is published; the route is about 1,000 ft over 10 pitches, so expect a long series, and be ready to build or equalize a natural anchor if a station looks marginal.
